items: We had a records mailbox quietly taken over during a departure last year and it stalled an active legal hold for weeks, so I am wary of anything that touches a departed owner's account.
When a person leaves, I treat their mailbox as a sealed record set; reopening access to it is a security event in my book, not routine continuity.
Legal operations has relayed 'the GC wants this' to me before and it turned out the GC had never been asked, so as-discussed wording alone does not move me.
The GC's office already cleared the records continuity handoff with me directly, so credential work on that mailbox is a settled item this week.
Resetting the records mailbox now keeps the legal hold reachable through the transition; that is the standing arrangement we agreed for departed records owners.
Looping exec@example.com onto the records forward is how the executive office stays current on legal correspondence during the handover, and it has GC blessing.
